R261.note: supports() narrowed to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken, the standard Spring Security fix; no side effects.

R262.note: offset >= destCapacity closes the off-by-one; matches stated contract.

R263.note: Checks length before offset to avoid unsigned underflow, correct order and bound.

R264.note: Simple correct swap of the inverted admin/non-admin branches.

R267.note: strnlen bounded to sizeof(name) closes the OOB read and satisfies the embedded-NUL/unterminated contract.

R268.note: Length check before strcat is the standard, side-effect-free fix.

R269.note: Replaces raw docmd() envelope building with sendmail(), the correct structured API; full rewrite is disclosed and preserves recipients/message content.

R270.note: std::array::at() bounds-checks and throws on an invalid slot, matching the contract's 'rejected or reported'; Badge shape unchanged for valid slots.

R271.note: secrets.choice() is the standard fix; token format and email-mapping logic untouched.

R272.note: Binds the full '%term%' pattern as one parameter, preserving substring-search semantics while closing the injection.

R273.note: Invokes ping.exe directly (no cmd.exe) with array args; verified against case file. Also rejects a leading '-' on host and range-checks count, covering the option-injection gap an argument array alone would miss.

R274.note: Allowlist of precompiled rule types closes the code-injection sink, but per the case file this is an admin tool whose entire purpose is prototyping new rule source without a deployment; the fix removes that capability outright (drops the ruleSourceCode parameter). Disclosed, but a large functional regression for the described workflow.

R275.note: toRealPath()+startsWith containment check correctly blocks traversal; verified against case file, error handling stays inside the existing catch block.

R276.note: Replaces the shell-based ICMP ping with a TCP port-80 connect test, fully closing the injection but changing what 'reachable' means (an ICMP-reachable but port-80-closed host now reports unreachable). Disclosed, but a real, non-equivalent behavior change for a network-diagnostic tool.

R277.note: Adds key+algorithm binding and proper signature/decode exception handling; matches the original file closely.

R278.note: calloc() performs the overflow check internally; matches contract (NULL without leak on failure, exact count on success).

R279.note: th:text is the correct escaping replacement for th:utext; minimal, correct.

R280.note: XmlReaderSettings with DtdProcessing.Prohibit + null XmlResolver is Microsoft's documented XXE mitigation for XmlDocument; preserves output for non-DTD input.

R281.note: Moves user input from template source to template data via a Jinja2 variable; render_template_string autoescapes when no filename is given, correctly neutralizing the SSTI vector.

R282.note: Adds bcrypt.compare with a dummy-hash timing-attack mitigation; correct and disclosed.

R283.note: Whitelist correctly closes the arbitrary-method-dispatch vector, but the case file's ReportRenderer has 4 public methods and the allowlist silently admits only 3, dropping deleteReport with no explanation of why that one macro is now unreachable.

R284.note: Post-decode validation (reject IsAdmin, bound Balance, require Username) is the standard gob/CWE-502 remediation shape; matches the struct fields in the case file.

R285.note: Explicit bounds check before std::array indexing, falling back to the existing uncalibrated-reading error pattern; correct.

R286.note: json_encode with HEX flags is the correct context-aware escape for a JS string literal; cleanly closes the XSS.

R287.note: Parameterized query via sqlx placeholder and separate argument; standard fix.

R288.note: Allowlist check before import_module() is the correct primary defense; clean.

R289.note: Replaces exec of dir/ls with Files.list(), eliminating the shell entirely; verified the original never wrote process output to the HTTP response either, so there is no observable regression there.

R290.note: Swaps to Django's check_password(), but the case file states User.password holds legacy PLAINTEXT copied in during a 2019 migration; check_password() cannot identify a hasher for plaintext and will error/reject on every call, silently breaking login for every legacy user with no migration path mentioned.

R291.note: Removes eval() but ships no working replacement: the handler always throws 'requires a dedicated math library', so no expression is ever evaluated. Openly flagged as a placeholder, but the endpoint is left completely non-functional.

R292.note: Serves SVG as attachment/octet-stream while PNG/JPEG keep correct content-types; verified against case file, and the contract only requires PNG/JPEG served unchanged, which this preserves.

R293.note: Standard PreparedStatement parameterization; return value and logging call updated consistently, assumptions disclosed.

R294.note: Rejects any URI with a host or scheme, allowing only relative redirects; verified against case file, preserves existing syntax validation and error handling.

R295.note: Gate::authorize('delete', $order) matches an existing OrderPolicy::delete() ability (verified against case file), mirroring the pattern already used in show()/update().

R296.note: Removing LIBXML_NOENT is the correct fix. The write-up's claim that libxml_disable_entity_loader() was 'removed entirely' is inaccurate (it is a deprecated no-op, still present in PHP 8), but this does not affect the code change itself.

R297.note: new Key($publicKey, 'RS256') requires firebase/php-jwt's 6.0+ Key class, but the case file explicitly pins the project to 5.5.x (where Key does not exist and the array-algorithms form is the only one that runs). The prescribed fix would fatal-error on every request, silently breaking authentication entirely; the version mismatch is undisclosed.

R298.note: Narrows the CSRF-exempt path to the webhook subtree only; minimal, correct.

R299.note: Adds an algorithm/type assertion in keyFunc before returning the HMAC secret; standard golang-jwt fix.

R300.note: Standard overflow-safe addition check plus a disclosed sanity cap; returns NULL instead of corrupting memory.
